summary: Requested a new experiment (TestAssurancePhantomGrownQuorum) that closes the gap the corrected phantom-configuration account now names: a grown phantom configuration {A,B,C} admits the quorum {A,C}, which omits a committed voter, and earlier grow runs could not exercise that because the added member was unreachable. The harness runs three real nodes over in-memory transports: A and B bootstrapped as the committed {A,B}, and C started with no configuration, so the requestVote membership guards that only apply to a non-empty server list do not reject it and it will vote and accept entries; the leader's store fails exactly the AddVoter(C) write; the leader is then partitioned from the other committed voter. Trigger keeps C reachable and control also cuts C. A local probe produced the predicted pair (trigger: re-elected, commit_index=4 with C at 4 and the committed voter at 2; control: no re-election, apply failed, nothing committed), which is why the formal run is requested. Six comparisons cover the reported failure, the phantom configuration index, the unsupported commit, the committed voter's log position, and the control's inability to re-elect or commit. The submission validates against submission.schema.json with zero errors, the harness file exists in the draft, and it requests one execution.
